grh_d82c67b57605f534cb0a.title: Fame Before Folly
paragraphs: A widely reported rescue suddenly turns Dr. Christian from a quiet country physician into a national celebrity. Reporters, photographers, radio calls and even movie offers descend on Rivers End, and publicity man Scoop Gordon convinces himself that the doctor needs professional management. When Dr. Christian refuses to spend his time posing and endorsing products, Gordon secretly hires a close look-alike named Bottomley and manufactures photographs that appear to show the doctor promoting everything from baby products to girdles and dubious advice. The false publicity soon creates angry calls and absurd accusations from people who believe the endorsements are genuine. Confronted, Gordon admits the scheme, and Dr. Christian makes him hear the unglamorous truth behind the original rescue instead of the heroic legend Gordon wants to sell. The doctor returns to his patients, relieved to exchange manufactured fame for ordinary work.

GRH catalogs [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]]'s "Fame Before Folly" for October 25, 1944, as episode 309. The structured record associates the broadcast with [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]]. Credited performers include Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Production credits include announcer Bob Anderson.
The surviving audio runs about 25 minutes. Sponsor associations in the structured record include [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].
